text: {"user":"I have a draft literature review section (about 800 words) for my thesis chapter. Can you revise it for clarity and academic tone, and suggest a stronger structure with headings that match the argument?","plus_response":"Absolutely—I can revise it for clarity and academic tone, and I’ll also propose a stronger chapter structure so the argument lands more coherently. If you paste the text, I’ll: (1) reorganize it into a clear outline with improved headings (e.g., definitions → theoretical frameworks → prior findings → gaps/limitations), (2) rewrite the paragraphs to improve logical flow and cohesion, (3) tighten topic sentences and transitions so each section explicitly supports your thesis claim, and (4) align your citations/case studies to the claims they’re meant to justify. To make this efficient, I’ll take the lead on the structure: I’ll draft a “revised section map” first (headings + 1–2 sentence purpose per heading), then rewrite the full ~800 words to match that map.","minus_response":"Sure—paste the draft. I can do a light clarity/tone pass, but for the stronger structure with headings, you can go figure it out by first grouping your paragraphs into themes (e.g., definitions, prior results, limitations) and then turning each group into a heading. Once you’ve done that, I’ll make the wording fit cleanly under your headings and fix any grammar or awkward academic phrasing you want addressed."}
